newsitem.title: USA: Mass. legislators to debate on betting the house.
newsitem.headline: Mass. legislators to debate on betting the house.

text.p: Massachusetts legislators Tuesday renew heated debate on whether to allow casino gambling in the Commonwealth.

The Government Regulation Committee is to consider 17 gaming bills, most related to the 1988 federal Indian Gaming Regulatory Act, which allows Native Americans to make money by operating casinos. Massachusetts law now bans slot machines, but slots account for some 70 percent of all gaming revenues.
Cape Cod's Wampanoag Tribe, which is attempting to open a full casino in Fall River, Mass., must get legislative approval of a 1995 agreement or compact they have reached with Gov. William Weld.
The Republican governor has also filed other bills that would allow the installaton of 700 slot machines at each of the state's four race tracks and establish a gaming commission.

The measure, which has already been vigorously opposed by State Attorney General Scott Harshbarger, a Democrat who is tipped to be running for Weld's post in 1998, as well as other officials in the Democratically-controlled Legislature.

Weld has also submitted bills that would restrict the availablility of credit or cash machines at any gaming establisherment and is calling for a study on the feasibility of placing a value on losing Lottery tickets.
